requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.index.chapter`. I derived the obligations from the requirement text and mapped each to the supplied tests. I did not request implementation source.

**1. Directive form (MAY, standalone, empty body, opening fence of at least three colons, closing fence at least as long).** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples]` covers these cases:
- A four-colon marker with a four-colon closer is accepted, and the matched range is asserted exactly.
- A five-colon closer on a four-colon opener is accepted.
- A three-colon closer on a four-colon opener is an error.
- A marker with no closer is an error.
- A marker with a non-empty body is an error.
- A two-colon marker is not a directive and is ignored.
- An inline marker, one that is not standalone, is ignored.
- A marker inside a code fence is ignored.
- A marker inside an `{req}` example block is ignored.

**2. At most one directive in a book.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[repeated_index_markers_fail_with_a_clear_error]` covers two markers in separate chapters and two markers in one chapter. Both cases assert an error containing "only one".

**3. Index lists all requirements from rendered chapters, each linking to its detail page.**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` asserts one table row per requirement. Each row links to `requirements-index/<name>.html`, shows the correct state, and has aligned columns.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers definitions in a nested subchapter and names containing dots, such as `cli.mdbook`. Its checks include the percent-encoded detail links and the detail page names and order.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` covers requirements spread across several chapters. It checks the resulting links and that the pages follow book order.

**4. When a directive is present, it is replaced by the table.**
- The explicit-index tests assert that `{requirements-index}` no longer appears in the index chapter and that the table rows are present.
- `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` asserts that `book.items.len()` stays 3. This shows the explicit index keeps its placement and no default chapter is appended.

**5. When there is no directive, the default chapter is generated (`requirements.index.chapter.default`).**
- `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` asserts the following:
  - The chapter is named "Requirements index".
  - It is at `requirements-index.md`.
  - It is the last top-level item.
  - It has no `source_path`.
  - It has no parent names.
  - Its number is `[3]`, one greater than the numbered chapter `[2]`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` covers a book with no definitions, both with and without prose. It asserts the chapter exists, has number `[1]` when no chapter is numbered, and has no source file. It also asserts that a marker inside a code block does not count as a directive, since the default chapter is still appended.

The detail-page obligations belong to `requirements.index.detail_pages`, which is cited here and is also tested separately. I found no obligation in the subject text without a test that exercises it and asserts its outcome.

text: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
